read_at_rule: Every time in this file is a fact about a past read. The satellite's own composite date is in each value's `t`; `read_at` is when this project read NOAA's grid. Nothing here states a cadence, a latency or a promise about the future.
nothing_derived_rule: Every `v` is NOAA CoastWatch's own value for its own cell in its own daily composite, and every `lat`/`lon` is NOAA's own cell centre. The only arithmetic in this file is great-circle metres between two published coordinates. There is no band, no threshold, no comparison and no clarity verdict here, and the light-depth estimate stays the app's own arithmetic, printed with its formula beside it.

caveat.quote: Daily Merge kd490 from NOAA-20 Visible and Infrared Imager/Radiometer Suite (VIIRS)
caveat.masking: A cell carries no value where the composite was masked. The product's own processing history names the mask (`cwcomposite … V2026257_D_N20_NRTNIR_US00_edgemask_kd490.hdf`) and the dataset publishes `l2_flags` (“Level-2 Processing Flags”) and `qa_score` (“QA Score”) beside every value. Cloud, sun glint, land and the swath edge are why a nearshore cell is empty, and they are why this file searches for the nearest cell that carries a value instead of reading the one cell a shore pin falls in.

caveat.quote: Visible and Infrared Imager/Radiometer Suite/Suomi-NPP NOAA-20 (VIIRS) Level-3 (WW00), Chlorophyll, DINEOF, Gap filled, MSL12,  Global, Daily, processed by NOAA.  EXPERIMENTAL.
caveat.masking: This product has almost no empty cells because a model filled them: DINEOF is a gap-filling reconstruction, so a value here may be interpolated rather than observed. The dataset calls itself EXPERIMENTAL in its own summary, quoted above, and this app prints chlorophyll as the plankton signal and never as a clarity measurement.

method.box_rule: A CIRCLE, measured in metres, and not a box in degrees: ±0.04° is 4.45 km of latitude but only 3.31 km of longitude at 42°N, so a degree box that sounds like 4 km is 700 m short of it due east at the north end of this coast. Kd490's radius is 4,000 m. Chlorophyll's is 7,000 m because its cells are 1/12° and half of one cell's diagonal is up to 6.56 km — a smaller radius could have no candidate at an entry point sitting squarely inside one of its own cells. `candidate_box_degrees` is only how candidates are gathered: a box that contains every one of those circles at every latitude.
method.cell_rule: For each entry point and each daily composite, the NEAREST cell inside the radius THAT CARRIES A VALUE. A masked cell is not a candidate, so a nearer empty cell never hides a further real one; a composite with no valued cell in the radius contributes no point at all. Every point carries `m`, the great-circle metres from the entry point to the cell that answered.
method.light_depth_rule: ln(10) ÷ Kd490 is NOT in this file and must not be. It is the app's own arithmetic, printed on the app's own card with the formula and NOAA's own caveat beside it.
method.t_rule: `t` is an index into `slices[<product>]`, which is the list of composite times this run read, oldest first. It is not a date this file invented.
